info.title: App AI Gateway API
info.description: A provider-native AI proxy for iOS applications and trusted server backends. Provider keys stay on the gateway; requests are checked, limited and recorded before they reach a provider.

servers.description: The cloud API host. On a self-hosted gateway, use your own origin.

CliPollProof.description: The initiating CLI's private operation token, distinct from the browser's approval proof.

GatewayBearer.description: A gateway access token, or an application API key for an issuer-less API-key app.

data.description: Machine-readable facts about this rejection, present only where the code alone is not actionable. A billing_request_quota_exceeded rejection carries periodId, periodStart, periodEnd, limit, used, and resetAt; a billing_plan_limit_reached rejection carries limit and used; an app_rate_limited or app_budget_exhausted rejection carries scope, one of user, install or app; a rate_limited rejection carries scope naming the endpoint policy that refused, plus limit, windowSeconds, retryAfterSeconds and resetAt.

jwks_url.description: An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.

verify_on.description: When the install's App Attest assertion is verified. every_request (the default): every gateway request carries X-AppAttest-Proof, a fresh assertion over that request; needs the AppAIGateway Swift package 1.4 or later. token_exchange: the assertion is verified once, when the hourly gateway token is exchanged, and requests carry only the token.

jwks_url.description: An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.

scope.description: Whose month monthly_usd is measured over: install (the default on App Attest applications) or user (the default, and the only value, on server applications). user on an App Attest application needs authentication.end_user.source issuer. Filled in on every parsed configuration.

provider.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. `constructor` and `prototype` are reserved.

kind.description: What the endpoint does, which decides the models it may serve: text, image, speech (text to speech), transcription (speech to text) or embedding. Must be a kind its api_style carries; defaults to the first of them (text for gemini_native). Filled in on every parsed configuration.

provider.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. `constructor` and `prototype` are reserved.

code.description: Stable identifier of what the warning is about.

message.description: What will stop, when, and what to do about it, in one sentence or two.

until.description: ISO 8601 UTC instant the behaviour stops.

id.description: The gateway-assigned id, and the `{app}` segment of every URL for this application.

warnings.description: Behaviour of this application that will stop on a stated date, computed when the application is read; empty when there is none. Read-only: tell the person who owns the app, and act before each date.

revision.description: Required: the revision the application was read at. An absent one answers 400 app_revision_required, a stale one 409 app_revision_conflict.

grant.description: How much of your role the key may use. `read` may list, inspect and validate but cannot change your apps, providers or settings: a change your role would otherwise allow is refused with `403 grant_insufficient`, and the key may still revoke itself. `manage` may do everything your role allows. Defaults to `manage`.

slug.description: The URL segment used under /proxy/{slug}/, unique across your providers.

secretHint.description: Last characters of a direct provider key; null when a shared provider gateway owns the token.

gatewayRoute.description: How this instance is routed inside its gateway. Always null for a direct instance and for gateways that take no routing configuration, such as Cloudflare AI Gateway.

baseUrl.description: Your own origin replacing the provider type's own base URL, stored canonicalized (https, public host, default port, trailing slash). Null means the provider type's own base URL is used. Always null on a gateway-routed instance, which cannot carry one.

route.description: Where this instance's traffic goes: direct to the provider's own API, or the type of the provider gateway it is routed through. Null when that gateway's type has no adapter in this deployment, so the instance can serve nothing until it is fixed or deleted.

apiStyles.description: The client APIs this instance can be called with on its route. A direct instance lists every style its provider type does not narrow; the provider itself answers for paths it lacks.

endpointStyles.description: The custom-endpoint styles this instance can back on its route.

modelPrefix.description: The namespace the route adds to model IDs on the way out. Clients always send the provider's own ID; null means the route sends it unchanged.

paths.description: Whose URL layout clients call under /proxy/{slug}/: the provider's own paths, or the one path per API style a gateway publishes for every provider it serves.

capability.description: What this instance can do on its route, decided by the gateway rather than re-derived by clients.

status.description: disabled is a reversible pause: the row keeps its secret, its pricing and its slug, and requests to it fail with provider_disabled until it is enabled again.

providerCount.description: Active provider instances routed through this gateway.

referencedCount.description: All provider instances referencing this gateway, including disabled rows retained for re-enabling. Deletion is refused while this is above zero.

install_id.description: The App Attest key id of the install that made the request, on App Attest applications; null for server applications.

api_key_id.description: Non-secret ID of the application API key that authenticated the request, including the client-proof key carried by an exchanged gateway token.

provider_gateway_id.description: The gateway connection that carried the request, or null for a direct call. Recorded for every routed request; the id is kept even after the gateway row is deleted.

provider_gateway_type.description: That gateway's type at request time, for example cf_aig.

credential_source.description: Whose credential paid, where something settles it: `direct` for an instance holding its own key, `byok` when a gateway serves it from your own key store or when a reporting upstream says your own key paid for the inference. Never inferred from a successful response; null when nothing settles it.

model_author.description: Who made the model, resolved when the event was recorded. An analytics dimension only — it never affects budgets or allowlists.

served_provider.description: The serving provider the upstream named, when it names one — the host OpenRouter routed to, for instance. Null means unknown, never a guarantee.

served_model.description: The serving model the upstream named, canonicalized back to the provider's own model ID.

reported_cost_usd.description: What the upstream said the request cost, on routes that report one. Null everywhere else; cost_usd stays the billed figure either way.

cost_source.description: How cost_usd was determined. `reported` is the upstream's own figure for this request, which is what was billed; `computed` is this deployment's price catalog; `unresolved` means the provider answered successfully but neither source could establish a cost, so the zero is unknown rather than measured. Null on events recorded before this field existed.

client_aborted.description: 1 when the client disconnected before the upstream finished streaming, which cancelled the provider call; null otherwise. Not a failure — the request was served as far as the caller wanted it — but an aborted stream often takes the provider's end-of-response usage with it, which is why such an event may carry cost_source unresolved.

daily.description: Authentication attempts per day, grouped by outcome and granular reason.

usage_failures.description: Provider errors per day from requests that reached an upstream.

rejection_samples.description: Sampled pre-provider refusals per day. These are diagnostic samples, not exact request totals.

success_rate.description: Null when the window contains no exchanges at all, which is not the same as a perfect score.

claim_delay.description: How long users waited for a required entitlement claim to propagate, over the window.

pending_users.description: Users currently inside an unclosed claim-propagation window — stuck mid-activation right now.

user_id.description: The verified issuer identity, where the attempt got far enough to establish one. Null for attempts refused before any identity was trusted.

outcome.description: `ok`, or the error code the client was handed — for example issuer_claims_missing, issuer_token_rejected, attest_failed.

reason.description: The granular cause behind the outcome, for example claims_missing, bad_signature, jwks_unreachable. Diagnostic only: clients never see it.

claim_delay_ms.description: Set only on the exchange that ended a claim-propagation window: how long the user waited from their first issuer_claims_missing rejection.

install_id.description: The App Attest key id of the refused install, on App Attest applications; null for server applications and for samples recorded before installs were.

scope.description: Null on historical samples whose limit scope cannot be recovered.

provider_slug.description: Attempted provider; this request did not contact an upstream.

post.summary: Exchange a client proof for a gateway token
post.description: App Attest clients send key_id, assertion, and challenge; the assertion is verified here whatever the application's verify_on, and the answer's verify_on says whether requests sent with the token must also carry X-AppAttest-Proof. Issuer-backed API-key clients send api_key and issuer_token. The verified issuer claim is always the resulting user identity.

get.description: On an App Attest application the request limits and, by default, the budget are the install's; install_id names it. Signed with X-AppAttest-Proof like every other request where the application verifies App Attest on every request.

schema.description: Required on every request sent with the gateway token of an App Attest application whose authentication.app_attest.verify_on is every_request; ignored, and never forwarded, where verify_on is token_exchange and for API-key clients. Format `v1.<timestamp>.<nonce>.<assertion>`: decimal unix seconds from the device clock (signed, but not compared with the gateway's clock), 16 random bytes as base64url without padding, and the CBOR assertion from DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion as base64url without padding. The assertion's client data is the SHA-256 of these lines joined by \n with no trailing newline: `appaigateway-request-v1`, the app id, the upper-case HTTP method, the URL path and query exactly as sent, base64url(sha256(body bytes)) (an absent body hashes as empty), base64url(sha256(the bearer token)), the timestamp, and the nonce. Missing answers 401 assertion_required; refused answers 403 attest_failed. The AppAIGateway Swift package 1.4 or later computes it.

blocked.description: Whether this user has been blocked in the console.

post.description: The path, body, and successful response retain the selected provider's native contract. For example, OpenAI clients send v1/responses or v1/chat/completions; gateway-specific provider slug quirks are never part of the client path. The gateway validates the configured path and model, spends one request from the account's monthly allowance, and streams the upstream response without buffering.

post.description: The endpoint's provider, model, fixed parameters, output cap, and fallback chain come from the application configuration, so you can change models without shipping a client release. The body is the one the endpoint's api_style takes, without a model: JSON for every style but audio_transcription, which takes an OpenAI audio transcription multipart body. A gemini_native endpoint streams when the request URL carries alt=sse, as Gemini's own API does; every other style streams as its body asks. The successful response keeps the serving provider's native format and streaming behaviour.

post.summary: Ask a person to log this CLI in
post.description: Persist the random token before sending: its digest is the operation's id, and sending it again answers with where the login stands — `completed` once approved, when polling or redeeming collects the key — and never hands the key over itself. Needs no credential. Open `url` in a browser, or show `userCode` for the person to type on the console's code-entry page; once a signed-in person approves, the CLI receives a management key of its own in the account they chose. Without `loopbackRedirect`, poll `pollCliOperation` until it completes: the first completed answer carries the key in `result.credential`, and no later one does. With `loopbackRedirect`, the approval page sends the browser there with a one-time `code`, which `redeemCliLogin` exchanges for the key; polling then never returns it. A login expires after 15 minutes, and its record is kept for a day. Each network address may ask for 20 logins an hour — sending the same token again is not counted — and may have 10 waiting at once.

post.description: The API of the console's OAuth consent page, which an MCP client's authorization request sends a person to. First-party browser only: both the request URL origin and the exact Origin header must match the console origin, and `submissionToken` is the proof from the consent page URL's fragment, so it never travels in a URL. Allowing, continuing without an account and denying each answer the `redirect` to send the browser to, and answer it again, byte for byte, when repeated with the same proof. Reading the details changes nothing. The client's name is its own claim, shown as declared by the host that served its metadata document.

post.summary: OAuth consent: continue without an account
post.description: The API of the console's OAuth consent page, which an MCP client's authorization request sends a person to. First-party browser only: both the request URL origin and the exact Origin header must match the console origin, and `submissionToken` is the proof from the consent page URL's fragment, so it never travels in a URL. Allowing, continuing without an account and denying each answer the `redirect` to send the browser to, and answer it again, byte for byte, when repeated with the same proof. Creates an account nobody has claimed yet, owned by the connection's own service identity, and connects the client to it with the `manage` grant whatever it asked for. Admitted where the deployment allows a new unclaimed account — always on the hosted service, where it is deleted unless a person claims it, and on a self-hosted deployment only while it is empty — and counted per network address with the CLI's account creation. Repeating it for the same authorization answers the same account.
